_comment: Out-of-sample state-program repeal reforms: neutralize a state credit variable and compare the simulated change in national state_income_tax (state credit variables are defined_for their state, so the national change IS the state change) to the state's official program cost. For a refundable credit the repeal effect equals total payments; for the nonrefundable portion it equals the amount used against liability, matching how revenue departments report claims. Restricted to programs with strong tax-year official actuals; the state_program_levels.json backtests cover the wider set. Washington's WFTC is levels-only: WA levies no income tax, so the state_income_tax measure would not capture its repeal.

reforms.name: Repeal Minnesota CTC + Working Family Credit
reforms.description: Combined credits (shared phase-out); benchmark is the House Research combined cost.

reforms.name: Repeal California CalEITC

benchmark.source: CA FTB EITC/YCTC/FYTC Report (Oct 2025), Table 1 p.8

reforms.description: One-year vintage gap: TY2023 actual vs the 2024 dataset period. Wiring note: ca_yctc survives this repeal — its eligibility falls back to the ca_eitc_eligible flag via the loss/limited-earnings path, whose threshold ($34,602 in 2024) exceeds the CalEITC earnings ceiling, so the measured delta is EITC-only (verified: repeal effect equals the ca_eitc baseline level exactly).

reforms.name: Repeal California Young Child Tax Credit

benchmark.source: CA FTB EITC/YCTC/FYTC Report (Oct 2025), Table 1 p.8

reforms.description: Gap analysis (2026-07 audit): +38.7% vs TY2023 splits into ~+5% benchmark vintage (max credit $1,117 TY2023 -> $1,154 TY2024; claims grew ~2%/yr) and ~+30% take-up — the sim pays every eligible unit and implies ~513k claiming units at the flat max vs FTB's 398,059 actual TY2023 returns (~78% implied take-up; CalEITC take-up measured at 54% among CalFresh-enrolled, California Policy Lab/JPubE 2023). A flat per-return credit passes the take-up gap straight to the total. Gap analysis (2026-07 audit): +38.7% vs TY2023 = ~6pp benchmark vintage (max $1,117 -> $1,154, phase-out start $25,775 -> $26,626: +6.2% measured on the same data) + ~30pp take-up. The model pays every eligible unit: 546-559k eligible units in the data vs FTB's 398,059 actual returns (claim/eligible 0.71-0.73, matching published take-up: CalEITC 54% among SNAP-enrolled per CPL/JPubE 2023). Per-unit amounts align ($1,025 sim vs $1,037 actual) — the gap is purely excess unit count; demographics ruled out (weighted CA under-6 is 6.2% BELOW ACS 2024). A flat per-return credit passes the take-up gap straight to the total.

reforms.name: Repeal Colorado Child Tax Credit

benchmark.source: CO DOR ORA, Individual Income Tax Credits TY2023

reforms.description: Vintage caveat (2026-07 audit): the TY2023 benchmark predates HB23-1112, which restructured the credit to flat amounts effective TY2024 (fiscal note: ~+$45.6M/yr, implying a TY2024 level near $135M). The 2024 simulation uses current law, so against the implied TY2024 level it runs ~14% UNDER; the +30% gap vs TY2023 is law-change vintage, not model error. Replace with CO DOR TY2024 actuals when published. Vintage caveat (2026-07 audit): the +30.4% gap is entirely law-change vintage, proven by replication — running the pre-HB23-1112 TY2023 law (60/30/10% of federal CTC) on this same data reproduces the DOR actual to the dollar ($89.2M vs $89,158,930), and the TY2024 flat-amount restructure (HB23-1112: $1,200/$600/$200 per under-6 child-dependent, $0-earners newly eligible) adds +30.0%. Against the bill's own fiscal-note-implied TY2024 level (~$135M) the sim runs ~14% under. Replace with CO DOR TY2024 actuals when published.

Repeal Maryland EITC

benchmark.source: Comptroller of Maryland, Income Tax Summary Report TY2024, pp.18-23

reforms.description: Benchmark sums the refundable ($410.1M) and nonrefundable ($140.8M) lines; repealing the take-better-of credit removes both. Wiring note: md_eitc itself is a derived reporting total (md_refundable_eitc + md_non_refundable_eitc) that Maryland's tax formula never reads — neutralizing it is a no-op on md_income_tax (proven: $0.0 repeal effect against a $475.7M baseline level). The repeal neutralizes both components on the tax path. Caveats: md_montgomery_eitc (county match on md_refundable_eitc, aggregated into state refundable credits) also drops, slightly overstating vs the state-only benchmark; the poverty-line credit's eligibility gate reads a separate component and does not expand under repeal, slightly understating.

reforms.name: Repeal Illinois EITC

benchmark.source: IDOR TY2023 final stratification p.1 (EITC $437,387,169) + IL GOMB FY2027 budget p.28 (IL CTC TY2024 estimate $50M): combined, because il_ctc = 20% x il_eitc is computed from the EITC and repealing il_eitc mechanically removes both

reforms.description: Illinois-resident returns; 20% match in both years. Entanglement note: il_ctc (from TY2024) is defined as a percentage of il_eitc, so neutralizing il_eitc removes both credits — the measured repeal effect ($491.4M) equals the il_eitc ($428.9M) plus il_ctc ($62.5M) baseline levels exactly. The benchmark is therefore the sum of both official figures.
